elements.text: Apertus Draft Gate
Technical report — Hack Apertus Online Hackathon, Track 2B. Team: Nick Menzi.
1. Summary

Apertus Draft Gate is a safety-first prototype for drafting a fictional workshop invitation email. A deterministic policy gate runs before the Apertus request. It sends only campaign-approved fields, retains the recipient address and internal note outside the model context, and produces a draft that remains pending human approval. The implementation has no email-send, CRM-update or messaging capability.
2. Architecture and deployment

The repository contains a fictional JSON fixture, a pure-Python policy module and a Docker-packaged interactive entry point. The policy rejects email, id and internal_note even if a faulty campaign lists them. The workflow first produces a data-minimisation preflight. Only after the operator enters y does it post the minimised JSON context to an OpenAI-compatible Apertus chat/completions endpoint. The output still contains no_send: true and pending approval.

Target architecture: on-premise. LLM_BASE_URL can point to an organisation-controlled, OpenAI-compatible Apertus inference service. The fixture, policy and approval logic remain local; the optional model request occurs only after explicit operator confirmation.
3. Use of Apertus

The configured model is swiss-ai/Apertus-v1.5-8B by default. Apertus is used for inference: generating a concise German email draft from a fixed instruction and an allowlisted fictional JSON context. The prompt prohibits invented claims and sending assertions. The model request excludes recipient email, record ID and internal notes.
4. Data

data/test_contacts.json contains two intentionally fictional contacts and one fictional campaign. It includes email and internal_note solely to test their exclusion from the model request. No real customer, mailbox, CRM, account, payment or contact data is used.
5. Evaluation

rows: Sensitive fixture data absent from payload
Endpoint failure returned as no-send error record

elements.text: The local suite was run with python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v. It makes no network calls. A live Apertus endpoint was deliberately not invoked during repository verification because no credentials or endpoint are stored in the source tree.
6. Limitations

This is not a production mail system. It does not score semantic quality, tone or hallucinations from a live model. A human must still review the exact draft, recipient and purpose. There is no approval persistence, authentication, HTML rendering, CRM integration or send path.
7. Reproducibility

Use Docker Compose for the interactive demo: copy .env.example to .env, configure an Apertus endpoint, then run make run from track_2b. The default answer exits after the safe preflight; y performs one model request with minimised fictional data. Run offline checks with python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v.
8. Next steps
Next steps are approval binding to a draft hash, structured red-team cases, an offline deployment recipe, human-rated evaluation data and an immutable, minimised audit log.
